binding.scope: All three literal records are positive human CLCN4–ABHD5 pairs in yeast two-hybrid assays. The array and prey-pooling records label CLCN4 as bait and ABHD5 as prey; the validated record labels both as neutral components. Tags and literal experimental roles are retained. These records do not establish an endogenous compartment encounter or a new CLCN4 regulatory activity.

propagation.mapping_scope: The initial MGI-form UniProt query returned HTTP 400. A successful mouse Clcn3 query independently resolves MGI:103555 to reviewed P51791. Official cross-references also resolve RGD:621219 to P51792, RGD:708381 to P51794, SGD:S000003801 to P37020, CGD:CAL0000179877 to A0A1D8PS75 and FBgn0036566 to three listed products. Current experimental records and repeated IBA records are distinguished; the historical PAINT tree/MSA/IBD placements were not reconstructed. Target self-inclusion is valid experimental grounding, not circularity.

arba.scope: Current target InterPro and FunFam conditions match sets 1 and 9 (zero-based); this authenticates the rule route, not the older channel interpretation.

reactome.scope: CLCN4 is an alternative catalyst-set member, not a consumed solute. The event consumes endosomal chloride and cytosolic proton and produces the opposite pools. The set is not a CLCN4/5/6 obligate complex. The broad pathway name does not override the explicit antiporter reaction.

terms.label: membrane
terms.definition: A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it.

terms.label: voltage-gated chloride channel activity
terms.definition: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a chloride ion by a voltage-gated channel. A voltage-gated channel is a channel whose open state is dependent on the voltage across the membrane in which it is embedded.

terms.label: chloride channel activity
terms.definition: Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of a chloride ion through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel.

terms.label: lysosomal membrane
terms.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding the lysosome and separating its contents from the cell cytoplasm.

terms.label: endoplasmic reticulum membrane
terms.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding the endoplasmic reticulum.

terms.label: chloride transmembrane transporter activity
terms.definition: Enables the transfer of chloride ions from one side of a membrane to the other.

terms.label: plasma membrane
terms.definition: The membrane surrounding a cell that separates the cell from its external environment. It consists of a phospholipid bilayer and associated proteins.

terms.label: antiporter activity
terms.definition: Enables the active transport of a solute across a membrane by a mechanism whereby two or more species are transported in opposite directions in a tightly coupled process not directly linked to a form of energy other than chemiosmotic energy. The reaction is: solute A(out) + solute B(in) = solute A(in) + solute B(out).

terms.label: recycling endosome
terms.definition: An organelle consisting of a network of tubules that functions in targeting molecules, such as receptors transporters and lipids, to the plasma membrane.

terms.label: recycling endosome membrane
terms.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a recycling endosome.

terms.label: chloride transport
terms.definition: The directed movement of chloride into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

terms.label: early endosome membrane
terms.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding an early endosome.

terms.label: late endosome membrane
terms.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a late endosome.

terms.label: endosome membrane
terms.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding an endosome.

terms.label: monoatomic ion transmembrane transport
terms.definition: A process in which a monoatomic ion is transported across a membrane. Monatomic ions (also called simple ions) are ions consisting of exactly one atom.

terms.label: transmembrane transport
terms.definition: The process in which a solute is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other.

terms.label: chloride transmembrane transport
terms.definition: The process in which chloride is transported across a membrane.

terms.label: chloride:proton antiporter activity
terms.definition: Enables the transfer of a solute or solutes from one side of a membrane to the other according to the reaction: chloride(out) + proton(in) = chloride(in) + proton(out).

ontology.scope: GO:0062158 is an active child of antiporter activity and chloride transmembrane transporter activity. It is not a chloride-channel descendant. Existing assertion IDs remain exact; refinements use proposed_replacement_terms. No NEW assertion or process is proposed.

products.scope: Both genuine seeded products are preserved. PMID:28972156 tested a long human construct and reported low expression and absent measured currents for a shorter 687-residue form under its conditions. No source isoform tags or universal short-form inactivity are manufactured.

primary_access.scope: Homology and cloning of a predicted 760-residue protein; no recovered full body or direct proton assay.

Human skeletal-muscle clone expressed in CHO cells; acid-activated outward currents reported. Full original Methods/Results not recovered, and later exchange refinement does not claim this assay measured H+ coupling.
Independent surface-pH measurements report active proton export. Exact ClC-4 construct and all Methods not inspected.

Actual original journal pages 424–426 Methods/Results and Figure 1/2 text inspected; ROOT additionally viewed page 425 pixels. Direct ClC-4 voltage-clamp/pH assays and controls establish exchange. Stoichiometry was only a rough estimate, not a precise 2:1 measurement.

Actual Methods lines 766–857, human HEK293 localization Results 963–1036, separate mouse fractionation 1154–1243 and Discussion 1966–2038. GFP/FLAG controls support ER localization; no panel pixels inspected. Its N-terminal targeting model differs from the later CBS-linker model.
Human WT/G544R constructs in HeLa and Xenopus assays; currents and ER-like localization, not independent proton-flux measurements. Selected paragraphs 33,48,49 and63.
Human variant oocyte currents are distinct from mouse neuronal knockdown/rescue and knockout morphology. Selected functional Results paragraph 42 and Discussion60.
Selected Methods20 and Results32–33 distinguish COS-7 localization and oocyte currents from algal structural modeling; several variants reduce current while Asp15Asn remains WT-like.

Human long ClC-4 with mouse ClC-3 variants; ER localization alone, partner-dependent endosomal/lysosomal/recycling targeting, mouse astrocyte host comparison and native-gel association. Currents alone do not measure proton coupling. Selected Results21–50 and Methods54/60/62.
